To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inrush current of a transformer can be calculated with high accuracy by solving the harmonic equations in a quasi-steady state.
the magnitude of the peak value of the inrush currents in single and three phase transformers is determined by the remanence of the transformer and the off-peak voltage.
inrush currents are determined by the initial bias and the external circuit, and not by the iron losses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the transient behaviour of transformers, especially of their inrush phenomenon and their dynamic performance.
the development of methods for the analysis and simulation of electromagnetic systems.

the following aspects: > - the inrush phenomenon is investigated using a harmonic domain approach, > - the influence of the remanence on the inrush current is studied, > - the inductance of a three-phase transformer is computed using a harmonic domain model, > - the computation of the inductance is extended to include the influence of the iron losses, > - the attenuation of the inrush currents is studied, >
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the harmonic domain approach is a powerful tool for the analysis of the inrush phenomena in single- and three-phase transformers.
the inrush current in a transformer is not an inrush current in the sense of a transient current but rather a quasi-stationary current.

, for the case of a transformer with no external circuit inductance, the inrush current is not affected by hysteresis and eddy current losses in the iron core and that the initial bias of the iron core is the only determining factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach for the simulation of the inrush currents in transformers.
we have shown that the inrush phenomenon can be investigated in an efficient and accurate way by a harmonic-domain computation, without having to solve a time-domain problem.
the inrush currents are a consequence of the remanence of the core and the initial voltage applied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inrush current is determined by a single quantity, the initial bias, which depends on the remanence of the core and the off-peak switching of the voltage.
a transformer inrush is not a transient phenomenon, but rather a quasi-steady state phenomenon that is determined by a sequence of quasi steady-state images.
the attenuation of the inrush currents in a single-phase transformer is determined by the total inductances of the circuit, and the resistance of the circuit.
